statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail holds the low band because December NQ at 31,026.75 is 234 points above the 30,792.50 session low inside a narrow 30,995.00-31,072.50 evening band, VIX closed at 15.41, and Thursday's 30-year auction cleared at 5.618% with a 2.54 bid-to-cover that pulled the 30-year yield back to roughly 5.60%. Stress stays elevated on a 3.4% semiconductor decline and crude closing near its highs.
recommendation: Tail at 17 maps to EA_ON, one point below the previous hour, because the long-end checkpoint that drove the 17:00Z reading to 28 resolved constructively: the 30-year auction drew a 2.54 cover with 72.3% indirect takedown and yields eased afterwards, while the evening futures session has held a narrow two-way 30,995.00-31,072.50 band and the 30,792.50 low is unchallenged. Stress remains elevated because WTI closed 3.6% higher at 91.49, Brent closed at 104.28 after reaching nearly 106, and the semiconductor complex fell 3.4%. The narrow danger window is set at 00:00Z to 02:00Z, covering the Tokyo and Seoul cash opens that price the OpenAI revenue revision and Thursday's chip de-rating for the first time. A chip-led Asian gap that extends without retracement, or a sustained break of 30,792.50, is the stated invalidation of this reading. Existing-position management and protective logic are unaffected by this mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow two-way evening band after a solid 30-year auction eased the long end, keeping Tail in the low band while a 3.4% semiconductor decline and crude near its highs hold Stress elevated
body: Cash NDX closed 30,725.81, down 434.27 points or 1.39%, a second consecutive decline from record highs earlier in the week, after a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is roughly 20 billion dollars below figures previously circulated. OpenAI reportedly told investors annualized revenue was approaching 50 billion dollars at the end of September against about 70 billion reported in late September; the gap is attributed to net-versus-gross treatment of cloud-partner revenue rather than a demand reversal. Semiconductors carried the de-rating: the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell as much as 4% before recovering part of the move to close down about 3.4%, with Arm, Intel and Marvell each off more than 6%, Micron down more than 5%, Oracle off about 5.5% and Nvidia down 2.9%. The rotation was narrow rather than systemic, with the Dow up 0.10% and the Russell 2000 closing flat. The long-end checkpoint resolved constructively. Treasury sold 22 billion dollars of 30-year paper at a 5.618% high yield with a 2.54 bid-to-cover and 72.3% indirect takedown; the 30-year yield then eased more than five basis points to about 5.60% and the 10-year settled near 5.23%, below the 5.28% H.15 reading for October 7. VIX closed 15.41, up 2.19%, a contained level for a 1.39% index decline, after an intraday high of 16.46. Energy remains the clearest Stress channel. WTI closed 3.6% higher at 91.49 and Brent closed at 104.28, up about 4% after reaching nearly 106, on Iranian proxy attack reports and Hurricane Isaias; oil largely ignored a statement that the United States would not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms, so the geopolitical premium has not decayed. In the evening futures session December NQ trades 31,026.75, up 0.18%, inside a 77.5-point 30,995.00-31,072.50 band after a marginal new high at 31,072.50 was retraced, leaving the 30,792.50 session low unchallenged. That two-way behaviour, the contained VIX and the orderly auction outcome are why Tail stays in the low band despite two declining sessions: the pathological no-retracement path the Tail score measures is not present. The shared Finviz context file was read and rejected as evidence because its payload is dated September 29 with a partial collection status, far outside the 90-minute freshness allowance, so this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources. The stated risk ahead is the Tokyo and Seoul cash open, which prices the OpenAI revision and the chip de-rating for the first time.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. The overnight stretch to 06:00Z held Tail between 10 and 14 with Stress drifting up from 47 to 55. Tail first reached the watch band at 07:00Z on a trend-down read at 22, held 20 to 23 through the European and early U.S. session, dipped to 17 at 14:00Z, and peaked at 28 with Stress 72 at 17:00Z around the 30-year auction, the only orange reading of the window. It unwound to 21 and 22 through the late session and returned to the low band at 20:00Z, printing 18, 17 and 18 in the three closing hours as Stress eased from 72 to 63. Confidence stayed in the high band throughout, between 85 and 89.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail inside the low and watch bands across all 24 hours, peaking at 21 twice. The first peak is the 00:00Z to 02:00Z danger window, where Tokyo and Seoul price the OpenAI revenue revision and Thursday's 3.4% semiconductor decline for the first time and a chip-led gap could extend without retracement. The path then eases to a 15 overnight trough through the Asian afternoon and close before lifting to 18 across the European cash open. The second peak is the 13:00Z to 14:00Z cluster, where a cash open following two consecutive declines coincides with the preliminary Michigan sentiment and inflation-expectations release. From 15:00Z the path assumes two-way price discovery and decays to 15 by the Friday evening close, with a 19 bump across the power hour for late-session reversal and weekend risk reduction. Stress declines gradually from 62 to 55 but stays in the elevated band throughout, reflecting the unresolved crude backdrop and AI-valuation repricing rather than observed index structure. Every reading beyond the current clock-hour is conditional.
